title: Spilling coffee can make you more likeable

lines.text: Making a mistake can make people like you more. But there's a catch.
In 1966, psychologist Elliot Aronson played students recordings of quiz contestants.
One was brilliant, answering about 92 percent of the questions correctly.
Another was average, getting about 30 percent.
On some tapes, the contestant then clumsily spilled coffee all over himself.
After the spill, the brilliant contestant was rated more attractive.
The average contestant who spilled? Rated less attractive.
It's called the pratfall effect. A small slip makes an impressive person seem human.
So if you're good at what you do, stop fearing the occasional mistake.

sources.claim: Aronson (1966): a highly competent contestant (~92% correct) who spilled coffee was rated more attractive; an average one (~30%) was rated less attractive

publish.description: A 1966 experiment found a small blunder made impressive people more likeable. But only if you're already good. The pratfall effect.
